requirement: GET a URL with aiohttp, retrying 429 and 5xx gateway statuses and connection errors with exponential backoff capped at 8 seconds and honouring Retry-After, while failing fast on other client errors.
skeleton: Retry status and delay constants, a Retry-After parser, and get_with_retry looping over attempts with raise_for_status on final or non-transient responses and an injectable sleep.
caption: Retrying idempotent GETs with aiohttp. RETRY_STATUSES is 429, 502, 503 and 504. get_with_retry(session, url, *, attempts=4, sleep=asyncio.sleep) raises ValueError saying attempts must be at least 1, then makes attempts - 1 retryable tries. A status outside RETRY_STATUSES goes through resp.raise_for_status, so 4xx such as 404 raise aiohttp.ClientResponseError at once, and a success returns resp.read(). A transient status waits for a numeric Retry-After header when present, otherwise BASE_DELAY 0.5 times 2 to the attempt, always capped at MAX_DELAY 8 seconds through the injected sleep. aiohttp.ClientConnectionError is retried the same way. The final attempt runs outside the loop with raise_for_status, so its ClientResponseError or ClientConnectionError reaches the caller. The fixture asserts, with a scripted TestServer and a recording sleep, that 503, 502, 200 returns the third body after sleeps 0.5 and 1.0, that Retry-After 3 sleeps 3.0 and Retry-After 100 sleeps 8.0, that three 503s raise ClientResponseError 503 after three calls, that a 404 raises after one call with no sleep, that a refused port raises ClientConnectionError after one 0.5 sleep, and that attempts 0 raises ValueError before any request.

plan.intent: Survive brief upstream outages without hammering the server
constraints: Only 429, 502, 503, 504 and connection errors are retried
Delays are 0.5 times 2 to the attempt, or Retry-After seconds, capped at 8
The last attempt raises aiohttp.ClientResponseError or aiohttp.ClientConnectionError instead of sleeping

rationale.teaches: Retry only transient failures, grow the delay exponentially with a cap, respect Retry-After, and inject sleep so the policy is testable.
rationale.why: Retrying 404s wastes calls, flat or uncapped delays either hammer or stall, and ignoring Retry-After gets clients rate-limited harder.

ops.docstring: Retry idempotent aiohttp GETs on transient failures with capped backoff.

candidates.why_wrong: Every error status is retried, including permanent 404s.
The delay never grows, so retries keep hitting a struggling server every half second.
A huge Retry-After is obeyed without the 8 second cap.
The loop runs one extra time, so a persistent outage costs an additional request and sleep.
The Retry-After header is ignored in favour of the fixed backoff.
